newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state sells 3.5 mln shares in CIGARETTE MANUFACTURER.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state sells 3.5 mln shares in CIGARETTE MANUFACTURER.

text.p: The Egyptian state sold about 3.5 million shares or 14 percent of monopoly cigarette manufacturer Eastern Company on Thursday in the second stage of the partial privatisation of the company.

The sales, to big investors willing to buy at least 10,000 shares, went through the stock exchange at prices between 96 and 102 pounds ($28.28 and $30.05) a share. The minimum bid price was set at 96 and most bids were in the range of 96 to 98 pounds.

"It was about 30 percent oversubscribed. The demand was quite strong given the recent correction (in prices on the Egyptian stock exchange)," said Elwi Taimour of brokers EFG-Hermes, one of the agents for the sale.

The owner, the state's Holding Company for Mining and Refractories, had offered at least 2.5 million shares. But it also said it would be willing to sell up to five million of the firm's total 25 million shares and an official at EFG-Hermes said on Tuesday his brokerage alone could cover that number.
The holding company owned 80 percent of the shares after selling 10 percent to the private sector in June 1995. The company employees own the remaining 10 percent.
The shares closed on the Egyptian stock exchange at 100.00 pounds on Thursday.
